title: Monotonicity of ordered vertex prefixes
statement:
Let $n\ge1$. Regard $\mathbf N^n$ as the exponent vectors of monomials in $\mathbf Z[Y_1,\ldots,Y_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Then write $u\le v$ for coordinatewise order on $\mathbf N^n$, $|u|=\sum_{j=1}^n u_j$, and $e_j$ for the $j$th coordinate vector. Let $D\subseteq\mathbf N^n$ be closed under addition by $\mathbf N^n$ and under $u\mapsto u-u_p e_p+u_p e_t$ for $1\le p<t\le n$. Suppose $a_1,\ldots,a_s$ enumerate exactly the coordinatewise minimal elements of $D$, in strictly ascending lexicographic order of $(|a_h|,a_{h,1},\ldots,a_{h,n})$. These are the additive monotone diagram and ordered vertex family of [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division], spelled out above. Then
$$D=\bigcup_{h=1}^s(a_h+\mathbf N^n).$$
For every $h$ and $p<t$ with $a_{h,p}>0$, there is $\ell<h$ such that
$$a_\ell\le a_h-a_{h,p}e_p+a_{h,p}e_t.$$
For every $0\le q\le s$, the set
$$U_q=\bigcup_{h=1}^q(a_h+\mathbf N^n)$$
is closed under addition by $\mathbf N^n$ and under $v\mapsto v-v_p e_p+v_p e_t$ for $p<t$. Empty unions are allowed; in particular $U_0=\varnothing$ and $U_s=D$.

source.place: Agent combinatorial refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997 section 8, Lemma 8.2 and Remarks 8.4, pp.274--275; Original proof Steps 1, 3--4: vertex domination and the degree/lex comparison after moving positive coordinate mass; closure extended to arbitrary vectors of a prefix orthant. No Stacks tag states this combinatorial result. ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13 supplies only the historical parent route; BM paper read online at https://mahalex.net/seminars/gabber/Bierstone-Milman%20Canonical%20desingularization%20in%20characteristic%20zero.pdf and absent from repository literature.

proof.text: Use the additive-diagram and ordered-vertex definitions in [def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division]. For $x\in D$, choose $b\in D$ with $b\le x$ of least total degree; the admissible degrees are a nonempty subset of $\mathbf N$ since $x$ is admissible. Any $c\in D$ with $c\le b$ and $c\ne b$ has $|c|<|b|$, a contradiction. Thus $b$ is coordinatewise minimal and equals some $a_h$. Conversely $a_h\le x$ implies $x=a_h+(x-a_h)\in D$ by additive closure. This proves the orthant-union equality, including the empty case.

source.place: Agent combinatorial refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8, opening definition p.273 and Lemma 8.2 proof p.274 (online PDF URL in source.place); ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, is historical context only.

proof.text: Fix $h,p,t$ with $p<t$ and $a_{h,p}>0$. Write $T(x)=x-x_p e_p+x_p e_t$. The hypothesis gives $T(a_h)\in D$, so Step 1 supplies $a_\ell\le T(a_h)$. Also $|T(a_h)|=|a_h|$. If $|a_\ell|<|a_h|$, the prescribed order gives $\ell<h$. Otherwise the inequality and equal coordinate sums force $a_\ell=T(a_h)$: all nonnegative differences have sum zero. The first coordinate where $T(a_h)$ differs from $a_h$ is $p$, where it is $0<a_{h,p}$. Hence it is strictly lexicographically smaller, so again $\ell<h$. This proves the earlier-vertex assertion.

proof.text: For fixed $p<t$, the coordinates of $T(x)$ are $0$ at $p$, $x_t+x_p$ at $t$, and $x_j$ elsewhere. Consequently $T(x+y)=T(x)+T(y)$, and all these vectors have nonnegative coordinates. In particular if $a_{h,p}=0$, then $T(a_h)=a_h$; if $a_{h,p}>0$, Step 2 gives $a_\ell\le T(a_h)$ with $\ell<h$.

source.place: Agent combinatorial refinement of Bierstone--Milman 1997, section 8, opening definition p.273 and Lemma 8.2 proof p.274 (online PDF URL in source.place); ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, printed pp.93--94, is historical context only.

proof.text: Fix $q$ and $v\in U_q$, and choose $h\le q$ and $b\in\mathbf N^n$ with $v=a_h+b$. For any $c\in\mathbf N^n$, $v+c=a_h+(b+c)\in U_q$, proving additive closure. If $a_{h,p}=0$, Step 3 gives $T(v)=a_h+T(b)\in U_q$. Otherwise choose $\ell<h$ from Step 2. Then $T(v)=a_\ell+(T(a_h)-a_\ell)+T(b)\in U_q$, since $\ell<h\le q$ and the difference is coordinatewise nonnegative. This proves closure under every required move.

proof.text: For $q=0$ the defining union is empty and both closure assertions are vacuous. For $q=s$, Step 1 gives $U_s=D$. If $s=0$ the same equality forces $D=\varnothing$, consistently with all preceding assertions. If $n=1$ there is no pair $p<t$ and the coordinate-move assertions are vacuous.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q20-a7ab7079f (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all five steps of the item and the cited def-trf-supported-homogeneous-division. The item's hypotheses (additive and move-closed D, vertices enumerated in strictly ascending degree-lex order) match that definition exactly, and the delivery has no new nodes. Step 1: taking a least-degree element of D below x gives a minimal element of all of D, which is some a_h; the converse inclusion follows from additive closure. Step 2: in the equal-degree case a_l = T(a_h), which agrees with a_h before coordinate p and is 0 < a_{h,p} at p, so it is strictly lex-smaller and l < h. Steps 3 and 4: T is additive on the whole vector, and every index prefix U_q is additive and move-closed. Step 5: edge cases q=0, q=s, s=0 and n=1 are handled. I tested D=N^2 with (0,1) < (1,0), where U_1 cuts inside an equal-degree block; D=N^n; D empty; and a non-move-closed counterexample showing the move hypothesis is needed. lem-trf-monotone-prefix-essential-restriction covers degree prefixes only and is not a duplicate.
